issue.title: Track JDK WARNING:Illegal statements to be fixed in quarkus or in upstream libraries

labels.name: kind/epic
labels.description: Large issue with links to sub-issues

issue.body:
### Description

This issue tracks libraries that need to fix some now considered abusing use of the OpenJDK classes.

A typical example

```
WARNING: An illegal reflective access operation has occurred
WARNING: Illegal reflective access by org.eclipse.yasson.internal.ReflectionUtils (jar:file:/Users/emmanuel/.m2/repository/org/eclipse/yasson/1.0.7/yasson-1.0.7.jar!/) to constructor java.util.AbstractCollection()
WARNING: Please consider reporting this to the maintainers of org.eclipse.yasson.internal.ReflectionUtils
WARNING: Use --illegal-access=warn to enable warnings of further illegal reflective access operations
WARNING: All illegal access operations will be denied in a future release
```

See https://quarkusio.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/187038-dev/topic/How.20to.20get.20rid.20of.20the.20ILLEGAL.20messages for some slightly more infos 

Essentially OpenJDK 11 went from not displaying to displaying once such error. With the intention to no longer run with such error in the future. Better start fixing things over time.

The strategy is to identify these issues one by one as we discover them and created a dedicated Quarkus issue for each linked back here in the epic list.
Then help upstream to fix things
In parallel, we could decide to mask these warnings for the issues we have identified and logged (and remove the masking when they are supposedly fixed).

Note that running with `--illegal-access=debug`,  will print the warnings on every illegal access that occurs during the run. Which would be a more effective way to find all culprits.

issue.title: Prevent 'illegal reflective access' problems when instantiating XStream

repository.name: xstream
repository.description: Serialize Java objects to XML and back again.

issue.body:
Relates to #101 and https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/10303#issuecomment-665308371

I realized that just by instantiating `XStream` a whole bunch of reflection access is performed by various converters (triggered via `Xstream.setupConverters()`).
**This is regardless of whether you will actually need the converter or not, just the setup triggers this.**

This PRs defers all the static reflection access by moving the respective fields and lookups to static inner classes which per JLS are loaded on demand in a thread safe way.
I also addded a test that analyzes the classes (via https://github.com/classgraph/). First I wanted to use ArchUnit but that requires at least JUnit 4 but Core still uses 3.8.1.

The most debatable change is the one to `AbstractAttributedCharacterIteratorAttributeConverter`.
I had to drop `readResolve` method and the `attributeMap` member. The map was `transient` anyway and `readResolve` puzzled me a bit, because the converter does not seem to implement `Serializable` at all.

With this PR I am not getting any `illegal reflective access` warnings anymore when instantiating `XStream` on AdoptOpenJDK 11.0.6.

body:
I took a stab at this upstream: https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/pull/216

This won't help for certain scenarios (e.g. if your parameter class contains a `TreeMap`) but it removed all warnings for my use case.

Now lets hope it gets merged and released soon.
That's great! Let's see what happens
Until a new release of xstream (which might take a long time), we _could_ work around this in Quarkus by registering our own list of converters. Just saying.
Yeah, if the release don't come soon, I'll let you do a PR for that :)

**Workaround** until then:
```
--add-opens java.base/java.lang.reflect=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens java.base/java.text=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens java.desktop/java.awt.font=ALL-UNNAMED
```
(yes, even AWT)
